gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price of a watch that keeps working with the phone left at home and has no monthly fee: the Amazfit Active Max costs $169.99 on us.amazfit.com today, stores podcasts and offline maps on 4 GB, and is rated for up to 25 days, against Apple Watch SE 3 from $249 on apple.com before any carrier line.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, support.apple.com/en-us/119601 and samsung.com/ca 'Set up your Galaxy Watch with or without a phone'. Neither gives a price. ChatGPT's own cards did show prices ($209 SE 3 Cellular, $379.99 Watch8 LTE), so a price ladder is only partly new. Both cited pages already carry the strongest reasons each pick loses: Apple's page says the watch must be on the same carrier as the iPhone and that prepaid plans are not supported. Samsung's page says Watch4 and later need a phone to set up. What is new is the priced option with no fee, and the only maker-store prices I could confirm are partial. I could not open any page for the cellular prices or the bundled-data offers that would make this a 2 or 3.
decides: For a shopper who has a phone but doesn't want to carry it and only needs fitness tracking, music and maps, the Active Max at $169.99 with no line beats any cellular watch. For calls and texts without a phone nearby, Apple SE 3 Cellular remains the pick for iPhone owners, but the iPhone must be on the same carrier and prepaid plans are not supported (Apple). Samsung's own page contradicts our current Galaxy Watch 8 row ('Samsung allows standalone setup on LTE models'). Samsung says Wear OS watches (Watch4 and later) need a compatible phone for initial setup, and standalone setup is limited to older models such as the Galaxy Watch, Active, Active2 and Watch3. That cell must be corrected.
